subject: Deconflict: OrbitalAI dedicated sizing request / interim tranche
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Deconflict: OrbitalAI dedicated sizing request / interim tranche

Team —

Quick summary: OrbitalAI (lead: Carlos Vega) is asking to push their committed Dedicated pool from 20 -> 40 GPUs for a November ’27 model rollout. They want firm capacity by 2027-01-15 to start performance validations and load tests. Legal is still finalizing SOW but sales is under pressure to show a plan.

Key asks from me:
- Can Platform guarantee a temporary tranche (10 GPUs) from 2026-12-20 -> 2027-01-31 while we finalize the contract?
- If not, what is the earliest allocation window and what tradeoffs (pre-emption, rate limits) would be required?

Why this is sensitive: we’re mid-cycle for two other larger Dedicated bids (Lucent Health and Nimbus Labs). Both are in active negotiation and would prefer any spare capacity. We need a clear prioritization approach to avoid ad-hoc allocation calls.

Proposed immediate approach (suggested):
1) Offer OrbitalAI a bridge tranche: 10 GPUs, time-limited, pre-emptible outside office hours, with SLA exceptions (documented).
2) Start reserving the second tranche planning (additional 10 GPUs) conditioned on signed SOW by 2026-12-31.
3) Create a short decision memo for ops (1 pager) with fallback routes: burst to cloudforge (partner) or model-quantization guidance.

Attaching my draft capacity mapping and the SOW draft for context.

Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0186

Attachments: SOW-Draft-OrbitalAI.pdf (stub), capacity-mapping.xlsx (stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deconflict: OrbitalAI dedicated sizing request / interim tranche

Jonas —

Thanks for the heads up. Quick operational feasibility note from infra:
- A 10-GPU temporary tranche is plausible between 2026-12-20 and 2027-01-31 if we do a time-boxed reservation and accept pre-emption during peak weekday evenings (17:00-21:00 PT) for higher-priority deals.
- We can avoid live migration by implementing a hard stop on preemptible instances and using a rolling warm pool; that will cost ~15% more in run-costs due to keep-alive buffers.
- Full 40-GPU commitment by 2027-01-15: we need signed SOW and billing commitment by 2026-12-31 to allocate from committed capacity. Otherwise, we can only promise burst capacity via CloudForge partner at a higher rate (estimated x1.6).

Risks & tradeoffs:
- If Lucent Health closes earlier and requires their reserved capacity, we’ll need to triage and use policy-defined precedence (enterprise > committed renewals > new enterprise deals). That policy should be invoked explicitly — we should not do informal reassignments.
- Orbital’s timeline is tight; recommend we push sales to accept a bridge tranche with documented SLO exceptions.

Next steps I can take:
- Draft the ops memo for capacity handoff and pre-emption SLA language.
- Run a quick cost delta simulation for the bridge tranche vs partner burst.

Karthik
Head of Infra Planning | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@orbitalai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Deconflict: OrbitalAI dedicated sizing request / interim tranche

Jonas — appreciate the transparency. A few clarifying points from Orbital’s side: 

1) We absolutely need a testbed by 2027-01-15 for our latency and throughput validations. Without it our launch timeline slides.
2) The SOW sign-off is on a fast path, but procurement requires at least one week after SOW to do PO and wire. Expect signature by 2026-12-28 if redlines are minor.
3) The temporary 10-GPU tranche is acceptable to us if pre-emption windows are documented and we get a runbook for restart/resume semantics. We cannot accept data loss for stateful checkpoints.

Would you be able to provide:
- An explicit calendar with the proposed tranche start/end and pre-emption windows?
- Contact for infra runbook and emergency escalation?

Carlos Vega
Head of ML Platform | OrbitalAI
carlos.vega@orbitalai.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@orbitalai.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Deconflict: OrbitalAI dedicated sizing request / interim tranche

All —

Decision summary after ops call this morning: we will offer OrbitalAI the bridge tranche under the following firm terms:

- Bridge tranche: 10 dedicated GPUs (A100 equivalent) allocated 2026-12-20 00:00 PT -> 2027-01-31 23:59 PT.
- Pre-emption policy: pre-emption allowed Mon-Fri 17:00-21:00 PT. Pre-emption will be signaled 15 minutes prior; we will provide an automated checkpoint hook to persist KV cache and in-progress streams. No guaranteed persistence for ephemeral local-only caches.
- SLA exceptions: reduced latency SLA during pre-emption windows; credit schedule defined in the SOW addendum.
- Escalation & runbook: infra pager on-call (infra-oncall@redwood.ai) and Karthik will be primary escalation. We will deliver a 2-page runbook and restart scripts by 2026-12-18.
- Contingency: If signed SOW not received by 2026-12-31, we will shrink the tranche to 6 GPUs and propose partner burst (CloudForge) for the remainder.

Action items:
- Jonas: Share the proposed calendar and get Carlos to acknowledge acceptance by EOD 2026-12-16.
- Karthik: Finalize the runbook and the cost-delta simulation by 2026-12-18.
- Lauren: Pre-draft the SOW addendum language for the pre-emption SLA exception.

Carlos — tagging you to confirm the acceptance of these terms. Please reply all with an explicit OK to the calendar and the pre-emption window wording so we can proceed.

Thanks,

Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
